# Requirements Readiness Checklist: NPC Generator

**Purpose**: Validate that the requirements in `spec.md` are complete, unambiguous,
consistent, and measurable enough to generate tasks from, across the generation walk, the
rules data and its licensing, reproducibility, and rendering.

**Created**: 2026-08-21

**Resolved**: 2026-08-21

**Feature**: [spec.md](../spec.md)

**Note**: This custom checklist is generated by the `/speckit-checklist` command based on
feature context and requirements.

**Review Ownership**: This checklist is a reviewer-owned requirements-quality review
artifact. Mark an item `[x]` only when the reviewer determines the requirements-quality
criterion is satisfied.

**Marker Semantics**: `[x]` means the criterion has been reviewed and satisfied for
requirements quality. It does not mean implementation work is complete.

**Scope note**: Several items below ask whether a rule that `plan.md`, `research.md`,
`data-model.md`, or a contract already settles is stated in the *requirements*. That is the
point of the question, not a claim the rule is undecided. A rule that lives only in a design
artifact is a rule no functional requirement binds, no success criterion tests, and nothing
stops a later change from quietly reversing. Each such item is resolved either by amending
`spec.md` or by recording that the design artifact is deliberately the only home for it.

**Disposition**: All 45 items were worked through on 2026-08-21 and every one is resolved.
Twelve new functional requirements were added, seventeen existing ones amended, four success
criteria rewritten, and two contradictions between statements in `spec.md` settled. The
resolution of each item is recorded beneath it. Where an amendment reached a design artifact,
that artifact was amended in the same pass; those are listed under **Consequential edits**
below. Two items (CHK007 and CHK008) were resolved against the source material rather than
from the existing artifacts; see **Source-material findings**.

## Requirement Completeness: The Generation Walk

- [x] CHK001 Is the rule that decides between the draft and the always-available fallback on a failed qualification stated, or do the requirements name only the two destinations without saying what selects between them? [Gap, Spec §FR-004, §FR-006]
  - **Was a gap.** FR-004 named both destinations and nothing chose between them. Amended: a failed qualification routes to the draft; a data-held count limits how many times one character may be drafted; beyond it a failure routes to the always-available career. The routing is now decided by a count rather than left to the generator's discretion.
- [x] CHK002 Are the requirements for what basic training actually grants documented: which table it draws from, how many entries, and whether a first career differs from a later one? [Gap, Spec §FR-007]
  - **Was a gap.** FR-007 required basic training to be taken without saying what it gives. New FR-007a: every entry of the career's service skill table at level zero on a first career, a data-held number of entries on a later one, both counts in data.
- [x] CHK003 Is a limit on how many times one character may be routed to the draft specified, along with what a failed qualification does once that limit is reached? [Gap, Spec §FR-004]
  - **Resolved with CHK001** in the same FR-004 amendment, and added to FR-038's constant list.
- [x] CHK004 Are the additional skill rolls a successful commission or advancement grants stated in the requirements, given FR-009 fixes the per-term count at one, or two in a career declaring neither throw? [Conflict, Spec §FR-009, §FR-012]
  - **Was a live conflict**, and the sharpest of the twelve. The source grants a further skill roll on each successful commission and each successful advancement; FR-009 read as though the per-term count were the whole rule, so an implementation following it literally would have produced under-skilled officers. FR-009 amended to state all four counts and to require all four in data, keeping the stricter reading reachable by setting two of them to zero.
- [x] CHK005 Is any restriction on attempting a commission in the first term of a career the character was drafted into specified? [Gap, Spec §FR-008, §FR-012]
  - **Was a gap.** New FR-012a states the bar and puts it in data; FR-008's term order now references it.
- [x] CHK006 Is an unmodified survival result that fails regardless of modifiers specified as a requirement, or does FR-019 read as though every survival throw is modifier-inclusive? [Gap, Spec §FR-019]
  - **Was a gap.** New FR-008a: an unmodified result at or below a data-held threshold fails whatever the modifiers, so survival stays a throw for a character whose modifiers would otherwise make it arithmetic.
- [x] CHK007 Do the requirements define what constitutes an aging crisis and how the debt amount it creates is determined, as distinct from stating that a crisis becomes a debt? [Gap, Spec §FR-021]
  - **Was a gap in every artifact**, not only the spec: `chargen-parameters.toml` carried the crisis cost with nothing anywhere saying what fires it. FR-021 now defines the trigger (an aging effect reducing a characteristic to the declared floor), the cost (a data-held throw times a data-held multiplier), **and** what settling the debt buys. See **Source-material findings**.
- [x] CHK008 Are the conditions that qualify a character for a pension, and the rule fixing its amount, specified, given FR-017 makes pension qualification the trigger for a separate benefit modifier? [Gap, Spec §FR-017, §FR-018]
  - **Was a gap concealing a defect.** FR-018 amended to state the minimum, the base, and the per-term increment, all in data, and to state that the terms are counted **in a single career**. See **Source-material findings**.
- [x] CHK009 Do the requirements define when a medical bill arises at all and what restoring a reduced characteristic costs, as distinct from the share the career's tier pays? [Gap, Spec §FR-024, §FR-025]
  - **Was a gap.** FR-025 amended: a bill is raised when a character leaves a career carrying an injury reduction, the employer's share comes from a throw against the career's tier, and the per-point restoration cost is data.
- [x] CHK010 Is a cap on how many benefit rolls may be taken as cash, or any rank modifier on material benefit rolls, stated in the requirements? [Gap, Spec §FR-016]
  - **Was a gap.** Both added to FR-016 and to FR-038's list.
- [x] CHK011 Do the requirements state that a career may carry more than one rank ladder and that a successful commission moves the character between them? FR-007 and FR-047c both presuppose a ladder without either establishing that a career has several. [Gap, Spec §FR-007, §FR-012, §FR-047c]
  - **Was a gap in the spec *and* in the career schema.** New FR-007b establishes multiple ladders, requires the career file to declare which is the entry ladder and which the commissioned one, and fixes what a commission does. The schema had no way to express this: `contracts/data-files.md` and `data-model.md` gained a `ladders[].role` field and a cross-file rule.
- [x] CHK012 Is the injury table a mishap defers to described in the requirements, given FR-024 reads as though the mishap row itself names the characteristics reduced? [Gap, Spec §FR-024, §FR-019]
  - **Was a gap.** FR-024 amended: a mishap may reduce directly or defer to an injury table, and a deferred injury is thrown for and recorded as its own step, so a reduction the mishap row does not name still traces to a throw.

## Requirement Clarity & Measurability

- [x] CHK013 Is "a narrow band of an equal share" quantified with a tolerance the automated check can fail against, rather than left as an adjective? [Measurability, Spec §SC-019]
  - **Was unfalsifiable.** SC-019 now fixes the band at ten percent relative: with seven regions, between 0.9/7 and 1.1/7 of the sample, roughly four standard deviations at ten thousand draws, so it fails on a weighting mistake and not on the dice. It also now *requires* the shipped tables to differ in size by enough that name-weighting would breach the band, which turns the old prose note into an obligation the check depends on.
- [x] CHK014 Does SC-012 state what is required when no locale with differing collation is installed, so that the criterion cannot be satisfied by a test that skips? [Measurability, Spec §SC-012]
  - **Was satisfiable by a test that skips on every machine.** SC-012 rewritten around two required checks: a guard that the library never consults the platform locale, which runs everywhere and carries the criterion alone, and the cross-locale comparison, which is now explicitly not sufficient and explicitly does not satisfy the criterion when it does not run.
- [x] CHK015 Do the success criteria state where and when the sampled audits must run, so a sample excluded from the routine test selection still counts as verified rather than merely present? [Gap, Spec §SC-003, §SC-019]
  - **Was a gap.** A preamble added to Measurable Outcomes: every criterion is verified in the complete test run, a criterion excluded from the routine selection for slowness must still run in the complete one, and a skipped check does not satisfy its criterion.
- [x] CHK016 Is "sources that publish names for general use" defined with a criterion a reviewer can apply to an entry, given SC-015b checks only that a source field exists? [Ambiguity, Spec §FR-043e]
  - **Was an adjective.** FR-043e now defines an admissible source (public domain, open data, government or census release, or a license permitting redistribution), forbids a source that restricts redistribution or whose terms cannot be established, and requires the recorded source to be identified precisely enough that a reviewer can find it and read those terms. The check stays a review one and now has something definite to apply.
- [x] CHK017 Are the lines of the Universal Character Format enumerated in the requirements, or must a reader obtain the source material to know what "its defined lines" names? [Clarity, Spec §FR-044]
  - **Was a reference to a document this project does not ship.** FR-044 now enumerates the five lines. A rendering SC-009 pins byte for byte cannot have its shape held only elsewhere.
- [x] CHK018 Is the content of the format's final line specified: what fills it, and the condition under which it is the omissible one SC-009 requires a reference for? [Gap, Spec §FR-044, §SC-009]
  - **Was a gap.** New FR-044a: the species-traits line is never emitted (every character is human) and the significant-property line carries the benefit items and is omitted when there are none, which identifies it as the omissible line SC-009 requires two references for.
- [x] CHK019 Are the ordering and repeat-collapsing rules for that line specified, given SC-009 pins the rendering byte for byte and FR-046 fixes ordering only for skills and careers? [Gap, Spec §FR-046, §SC-009]
  - **Was a gap.** FR-046 gained the benefit line: same separator as the skills, repeats collapsed to name and count, sorted by the same locale-independent key.
- [x] CHK020 Is the separator between an attached rank title and the name specified, along with the form the line takes when the character holds no title? [Gap, Spec §FR-047, §FR-047c]
  - **Was a gap.** FR-047 now fixes title, single space, name; and an untitled character's line beginning with the name and no leading separator.
- [x] CHK021 Does FR-048a state the batch-of-one identity in terms a test can check, rather than by reference to "the single character of that seed and position", which restates the claim it is making? [Clarity, Spec §FR-048a]
  - **Was circular.** Reworded: rendering a batch of one produces exactly the bytes that rendering the single character generated from the same seed produces, with no separator before or after. The character-level property behind it is now in FR-057; see CHK031.

## Requirement Consistency & Conflicts

- [x] CHK022 Do the requirements use "career already entered" and "career already served" consistently wherever they gate re-entry and accumulate the qualification penalty? A character drafted into a career and mishapped out of it in one term entered it, and the two readings differ for exactly that character. [Conflict, Spec §FR-015]
  - **Was inconsistent.** The source says both, and `research.md` R10 settled on "entered" without the spec following. FR-015, its edge case, and FR-038 now all say "entered", FR-015 says why, and a new Assumptions entry records the resolution.
- [x] CHK023 Do the two statements about a characteristic below the pseudo-hex range resolve against each other: "the reduction is applied and recorded, no death results" against "a score outside the declared range fails the run naming the score and the range"? [Conflict, Spec §Edge Cases]
  - **Was a genuine contradiction between two edge cases in this document.** Read together they required the letters to cover negative scores, which no notation supplies. Replaced with three bullets that agree: a reduction floors at the declared bottom (recording both the reduction called for and the amount applied), a floored characteristic stands with no death, and only a score above the top fails the run.
- [x] CHK024 Does FR-042's requirement that the notice chain be "widened" describe what the designation split actually requires of a notice that today claims every data file under the data root? [Conflict, Spec §FR-042, §FR-042a]
  - **The requirement described the opposite of the required change.** The chain claims every data file, so covering the new OGC files needs no widening at all; excluding the name tables needs a narrowing. FR-042 now says "adjusted... so that it covers every Open Game Content file and nothing else", states that the adjustment is a narrowing, and says why. This is the item most likely to have shipped a licensing defect.
- [x] CHK025 Does SC-008's "all three medical tiers" agree with FR-037's placing the tier definitions in data a referee may extend or reduce? [Consistency, Spec §FR-037, §SC-008]
  - **Was a criterion contradicting the requirement it checked.** SC-008 now reads "every medical tier the shipped data declares" and says why it counts from the data. The same defect was found and fixed in User Story 1's first acceptance scenario, which said "six characteristics" where FR-002 makes the set data.
- [x] CHK026 Are the deliberate departures from the source material enumerated in the requirements (the term cap overriding a natural re-enlistment result, the mishap term's year cost, the specific benefit-count rule), or does the spec record only the departures it happens to have noticed? [Traceability, Spec §Assumptions, §FR-014, §FR-020]
  - **Was scattered.** A new Assumptions block enumerates them as departures rather than leaving them as isolated readings: no character dies, a characteristic floors, a mishap term costs two years, a natural re-enlistment result does not override the cap, noble titles are not rendered, gender is not modeled. Collected so review can tell a departure from an oversight and a later feature does not "fix" one back.
- [x] CHK027 Do FR-029 and FR-047d between them enumerate every field the character carries, including the rank title that FR-050 requires machine-readable output to emit unconditionally? [Completeness, Spec §FR-029, §FR-047d, §FR-050]
  - **Was incomplete.** FR-029 was missing the title and the character's own seed, both of which the JSON contract emits. Both added, the list declared exhaustive, and FR-047d now requires the title carried as its own field and not as part of the name string, so SC-018's field-by-field comparison has a field rather than a prefix to strip.

## Reproducibility & Determinism

- [x] CHK028 Do the requirements state whether a seed reproduces the same character across package versions, and does anything warn a referee quoting a seed that it does not? SC-001 fixes the version; nothing states the consequence of changing it. [Gap, Spec §FR-056, §SC-001]
  - **Was a gap.** New FR-056b states that a seed promises nothing across versions and requires any change to the draw order to be flagged in the changelog as breaking. SC-001's "one package version" had been assuming this without saying it.
- [x] CHK029 Is it stated that the order of draws in the walk is itself part of the reproducibility contract, so that reordering two independent draws is a breaking change rather than an internal refactor? [Gap, Spec §FR-056, §FR-023]
  - **Resolved with CHK028** in FR-056b, which is where `research.md` R1's "consequence to guard" now has a requirement binding it.
- [x] CHK030 Does FR-056a state the property it requires, that supplying a name leaves the rest of the character untouched, independently of any particular arrangement of the name draw? [Clarity, Spec §FR-056a, §FR-047b]
  - **Mostly satisfied, tightened.** Reworded so the property leads (identical in every field but the name and its parts) and the failure mode follows as illustration rather than as the requirement.
- [x] CHK031 Is the requirement that a batch of one and a single-character run produce the same person stated as a property of the characters, rather than only as a property of their rendered bytes? [Gap, Spec §FR-048a, §FR-050a]
  - **Was stated only for bytes.** FR-057 now states the character-level identity, and FR-048a's rendered consequence follows from it. Without this the requirement was testable only through a renderer.
- [x] CHK032 Do the requirements specify what happens when no seed is supplied, and whether that path is exempt from the reproducibility requirements? [Gap, Spec §FR-053, §FR-056]
  - **Was a gap.** New FR-053b: a seed is drawn from outside the seeded generator, reported wherever a seed is reported, and named as the one point exempt from FR-056, with the exemption's purpose stated, since it is what makes omitting the seed useful.

## Rendering & Output

- [x] CHK033 Do the requirements specify whether a caller-supplied name also receives the rank title, or only a rolled one? [Ambiguity, Spec §FR-047, §FR-047b]
  - **Was ambiguous.** FR-047 now says the title attaches either way: it is a fact about the career served, not about how the character came to be named.
- [x] CHK034 Is it specified which seed text mode reports on standard error for a batch, and whether the per-character derived seeds appear there at all? [Clarity, Spec §FR-051, §FR-050a]
  - **Was ambiguous.** FR-051 said "the seed", singular, of a run that may produce twelve. It now says the master seed and only the master seed, and forbids the derived seeds on standard error.
- [x] CHK035 Do the requirements state how a request for both machine-readable output and the fuller text rendering resolves, given FR-053 lists the two choices without saying they interact? [Gap, Spec §FR-053, §FR-049, §FR-050]
  - **Was a gap.** New FR-053d: accepted, changes nothing, because FR-050 already emits everything. It also records why this is accepted where `as_text(throw, full=True)` is refused: both readings here deliver everything, so there is no wrong outcome to protect against.
- [x] CHK036 Do the requirements state that the fuller rendering's history line is composed at render time from the step's parts, in a form a test can distinguish from a stored prose field that happens to look composed? [Measurability, Spec §FR-030a, §FR-049]
  - **Was unfalsifiable as written.** FR-030a now forbids any field of a step holding a line composed from the step's other parts, which makes the property checkable from the record's shape rather than by someone judging whether a stored string looks composed.

## Data, Schema & Licensing

- [x] CHK037 Is the requirement that no two surname tables in force declare the same region stated? FR-043f weights per table, so a duplicated region takes a double share and nothing in the requirements forbids it. [Gap, Spec §FR-043c, §FR-043f]
  - **Was a gap** the design had caught and the requirements had not. New FR-043j forbids it, failing the run and naming both files. The silent double-share is exactly the failure mode FR-043f exists to prevent.
- [x] CHK038 Are the requirements defined for a data set in which no surname table is in force at all, as distinct from FR-043h's empty table? [Gap, Edge Case, Spec §FR-043f, §FR-043h]
  - **Resolved with CHK037** in FR-043j, plus an edge case covering both conditions.
- [x] CHK039 Does FR-039 name every fact the characteristics registry must gain, including whatever the aging and mishap tables need in order to select characteristics by class from data rather than from engine code? [Completeness, Spec §FR-039]
  - **Was incomplete.** `research.md` R12 had recorded the characteristic class as a rule the requirements imply but do not name, precisely so it would not pass as a design liberty. FR-039 now names it, along with the bottom of the pseudo-hex range, and states why the class is load-bearing.
- [x] CHK040 Does FR-038's enumerated list cover the constants the walk actually needs, or does "at minimum" leave a rules constant that SC-013 would not catch sitting in engine code? [Completeness, Spec §FR-038, §SC-013]
  - **"At minimum" was doing real damage.** The contract's parameter file held roughly a dozen constants FR-038 did not reach, so SC-013 could pass with any of them in code. FR-038 now enumerates the full list, drops "at minimum", and states that a constant the walk needs which is absent from the list is a defect in the requirement itself.
- [x] CHK041 Is it clear in the requirements that an override file is held to neither licensing designation, so a house-rule file is not required to carry a header it has no basis to carry? [Clarity, Spec §FR-042, §FR-042a]
  - **Was stated in the contract only.** FR-042 now says it, with the reason: the obligations are about what this project redistributes, and a house rule redistributes nothing.
- [x] CHK042 Is the requirement stated that every characteristic class a chargen table names must resolve against the characteristics registry, so a class naming nothing fails the load rather than silently performing no effect? [Gap, Spec §FR-040, §FR-043]
  - **Was a gap.** New FR-040a. The failure it prevents is the worst kind available here: a wrong character rather than a failed run.

## Scenario & Edge Case Coverage

- [x] CHK043 Are the requirements defined for a caller-supplied name that is empty, given FR-047 requires every character to have a personal name and requires a supplied name verbatim? [Gap, Edge Case, Spec §FR-047, §FR-047d]
  - **Was a gap** where two requirements pulled against each other. New FR-053c makes it a usage error, with an edge case recording why rolling a name instead was rejected: it makes an empty string mean the opposite of what it says.
- [x] CHK044 Do the requirements state what the library does with a name supplied alongside a count above one, given FR-053a states the rule as a command-line usage error while FR-055 requires every capability reachable without the command line? [Gap, Spec §FR-053a, §FR-055]
  - **Was a gap.** FR-053a now makes the refusal a property of the capability: the library rejects it on the same terms and the command reports it as a usage error. A rule enforced only at the command line is one a library consumer does not get.
- [x] CHK045 Are the requirements for a failed run's streams defined: that standard output carries nothing at all rather than a partial sheet or a sheet with a caveat? [Coverage, Exception Flow, Spec §FR-051, §FR-054]
  - **Was stated in the CLI contract only.** FR-054 now requires it, tying it to the commitment FR-051 already makes for a successful run: a redirected failure produces an empty file, not something that reads as a character sheet.

## Source-material findings

Two items could not be resolved from the existing artifacts and were settled against the
source material directly. Both changed a rule rather than only its wording.

1. **A pension is earned in a single career** (CHK008). The source says "5 or more terms in a
   single service". FR-018 and `pension.minimum-terms` as first written compared a threshold
   against a term count with nothing saying which term count, and the natural implementation
   sums the character's terms across all careers. That reading pays a character with three
   terms in each of two careers a pension neither career owes them. The requirement, the
   contract's key note, SC-004's audit, and a new edge case now all say "in a single career".
2. **Settling an aging-crisis debt restores the characteristics** (CHK007). The source's
   payment buys medical care that brings the affected characteristics back up. The
   always-living reading turns the payment into a debt, which changes *when* it is paid and
   not *what it is for*, but no artifact said so, so an implementation could have recorded the
   debt, settled it, and restored nothing while passing every arithmetic check. FR-021 now
   states it, and `chargen-parameters` gained `medical.crisis-restores-to`, shipped at 1,
   rather than the engine holding the restored score.

## Consequential edits

Amendments that reached beyond `spec.md`, made in the same pass so the artifacts do not drift:

- `contracts/data-files.md`: `ladders[].role` added to the career schema with its validation
  rule (CHK011); `medical.crisis-restores-to` added to the chargen parameters; key notes added
  for the pension's single-career reading and the aging-crisis trigger; two cross-file rules
  added.
- `data-model.md`: `CareerDefinition.ladders` no longer listed as unchanged; two cross-file
  rules added.
- `plan.md`: the requirement count corrected from 58 to 89; four new entries in **Traps worth
  naming now**, covering the single-career pension, the ladder move on commission, what
  settling a crisis debt buys, and the ordering of debt settlement.

## Notes

- Mark items `[x]` only after review confirms the requirement-quality criterion is satisfied
- Leave items unchecked when they still require clarification, correction, or reviewer evaluation
- `/speckit-implement` reads checklist checkbox state as a gate and must not modify markers
- `checklists/requirements.md` has a separate built-in lifecycle maintained by `/speckit-specify` and `/speckit-clarify`
- Items are numbered sequentially for easy reference
